chunks: ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father, from Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā, from Yūnus, from Ibn Miskān, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:
The diyah of a Jew, a Christian, and a Magian is eight hundred dirhams.

key_terms.النَّصْرَانِيِّ: a Christian, mentioned here in the legal ruling on diyah
key_terms.الْمَجُوسِيِّ: a Magian (Zoroastrian), included here in the same legal category
key_terms.الْيَهُودِيِّ: a Jew, mentioned here as one of the protected non-Muslim groups under discussion
key_terms.دِرْهَمٍ: dirhams; a monetary unit used for legal compensation
key_terms.دِيَةُ: blood-money; legal financial compensation for killing or bodily harm

ai.seo_question: What is the diyah of a Jew, Christian, or Magian in this hadith from Tahdhib al-Ahkam?
ai.summary: This hadith states a legal ruling concerning the diyah for certain non-Muslim groups: Jews, Christians, and Magians. It belongs to the jurisprudential discussions of retaliation and compensatory blood-money in Islamic law.
